answer:
The longest‑lasting dynasty in Chinese history is the **Zhou dynasty** (c. 1046 – 256 BCE, about 790 years).  
Its founding monarch was **King Wu of Zhou** (Ji Fa), who overthrew the last Shang king at the Battle of Muye and began the Zhou reign.

He is recorded in the “Kings” section of the Zhou article and in the “Founding and Rise” section of the Preceden timeline.  - During King Wu’s reign, the Zhou royal house carried the surname **Ji**, and his successors ruled the Western Zhou until the capital was moved to Wangcheng (Optionally mention him as first king).  These facts confirm the earlier deduction that the Zhou dynasty is the longest in antiquity and that its inaugural ruler was King Wu of Zhou.
